_comment: Techniques listed here are deliberately excluded from coverage-gap reporting. Each entry needs a real reason - 'not observable via internal log sources' is only valid when it's actually true, checked against what the technique describes, not applied as a blanket excuse to avoid work. Reference: this file is checked against mitre_reference.json by coverage_gap_report.py - an ID here that doesn't exist in the reference is flagged as an error, not silently ignored.

out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1583: Acquire Infrastructure - attacker acquires their own domains/servers, entirely outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1584: Compromise Infrastructure - attacker compromises a THIRD PARTY's infrastructure to use as their own, outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1585: Establish Accounts - attacker creates accounts on external platforms (social media, email providers) for later use, outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1586: Compromise Accounts - attacker compromises a THIRD PARTY's accounts for later use, outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1587: Develop Capabilities - attacker builds their own malware/tools, outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1588: Obtain Capabilities - attacker acquires tools/malware/exploits from elsewhere, outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1608: Stage Capabilities - attacker uploads tools to their own staged infrastructure, outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1650: Acquire Access - attacker purchases access from an access broker, a transaction outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1683: Generate Content - attacker uses AI tools to generate phishing/deepfake content, outside the victim's environment
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1589: Gather Victim Identity Information - external OSINT research about the org's people, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1590: Gather Victim Network Information - external OSINT/passive DNS research about the org's network, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1591: Gather Victim Org Information - external OSINT research about the org itself, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1592: Gather Victim Host Information - external OSINT/fingerprinting research about specific hosts, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1593: Search Open Websites/Domains - attacker searches public websites/social media, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1594: Search Victim-Owned Websites - attacker browses the org's own public website for info, largely indistinguishable from normal traffic and not meaningfully observable as a distinct technique via internal logs
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1596: Search Open Technical Databases - attacker searches public technical databases (WHOIS, certificate transparency logs, etc.), not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1597: Search Closed Sources - attacker purchases/searches closed threat intel or breach data sources, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1681: Search Threat Vendor Data - attacker searches published vendor threat intel about the target, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1682: Query Public AI Services - attacker queries public AI services for recon assistance, not observable internally
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.001: Binary Padding - requires static file analysis (file size/content inspection) to detect, not observable via typical event logging
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.002: Software Packing - requires static or dynamic binary analysis to detect a packed executable, not observable via typical event logging
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.003: Steganography - requires deep content/statistical analysis of files to detect hidden data, not observable via typical event logging
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.005: Indicator Removal from Tools - describes the attacker modifying their OWN malware before use, an action that happens outside the victim's environment before delivery
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.007: Dynamic API Resolution - an internal malware runtime behavior (resolving Windows API calls at runtime to avoid static import-table analysis), not observable via typical event logging without specialized behavioral/memory analysis tooling
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.008: Stripped Payloads - requires static binary analysis (checking for stripped symbol/debug information) to detect, not observable via typical event logging
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.009: Embedded Payloads - requires static file content analysis (extracting an embedded payload from a carrier file) to detect, not observable via typical event logging
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.012: LNK Icon Smuggling - requires deep .lnk file structure inspection to detect, not observable via typical event logging
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.014: Polymorphic Code - an internal malware self-modification behavior, not observable via typical event logging without specialized behavioral/memory analysis tooling
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.016: Junk Code Insertion - requires static binary/disassembly analysis to detect, not observable via typical event logging
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.017: SVG Smuggling - requires deep content inspection of SVG file payloads; no specific verified log source evidence found for this catalog
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1027.006: HTML Smuggling - requires deep content inspection of HTML/JS payloads; no specific verified log source evidence found for this catalog
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1497: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion - malware checking its own execution environment (VM artifacts, user activity, elapsed time) before deciding whether to act. This is an internal decision made by the malicious process itself, not an event that standard endpoint telemetry (process creation, file, registry monitoring) logs.
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1497.001: System Checks - same reasoning as parent T1497: an internal pre-execution self-check, not a logged event
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1497.002: User Activity Based Checks - same reasoning as parent T1497: an internal pre-execution self-check, not a logged event
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1497.003: Time Based Checks - same reasoning as parent T1497: an internal pre-execution self-check, not a logged event
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1622: Debugger Evasion - malware checking for the presence of a debugger before deciding whether to act, an internal pre-execution self-check rather than a logged event
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1040: Network Sniffing - requires packet capture capability to detect an adversary passively capturing traffic; not something standard endpoint or infrastructure event logs (process creation, file, registry) provide visibility into
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1665: Hide Infrastructure - describes the attacker managing/rotating their OWN C2 infrastructure (IP rotation, CDN fronting, etc.) to evade takedown or tracking. This is attacker-side infrastructure management, not an action observable within the victim's environment - the same reasoning as the Resource Development tactic.
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1011: Exfiltration Over Other Network Medium - by definition uses a network medium separate from the one the organization's monitored infrastructure covers (e.g. a rogue cellular modem), so it falls outside what any source in this catalog could observe
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1495: Firmware Corruption - requires hardware-level firmware integrity checking (e.g. TPM attestation) to detect, which is a fundamentally different monitoring capability than the event-log-based sources in this catalog
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1669: Wi-Fi Networks - requires wireless spectrum/AP monitoring (rogue access point detection) to observe, a fundamentally different monitoring capability than the wired-network and endpoint sources in this catalog
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1542: Pre-OS Boot - bootkit/firmware-level tampering (MBR, BIOS/UEFI, TFTP boot) requires hardware-level boot integrity checking, the same fundamentally different monitoring capability noted for T1495 Firmware Corruption
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1480: Execution Guardrails - malware checking environmental conditions (domain membership, IP range, etc.) before deciding whether to run, an internal pre-execution self-check rather than a logged event - same reasoning as T1497 and T1622
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1678: Delay Execution - malware sleeping or delaying before running to evade sandboxes, an internal pre-execution behavior rather than a logged event - same reasoning as T1497 and T1622
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1679: Selective Exclusion - malware selectively avoiding specific systems or users, an internal decision the malicious process makes rather than a logged event
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1557.004: Evil Twin - rogue Wi-Fi access point impersonation requires wireless spectrum/AP monitoring, the same fundamentally different monitoring capability already noted for T1669 Wi-Fi Networks
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1001.002: Steganography - requires statistical/content analysis of files or network payloads to detect hidden data, not observable via typical event logging - same reasoning as T1027.003
out_of_scope.enterprise-attack:T1195.003: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain - physical hardware tampering during manufacturing/shipping, occurs entirely outside the victim's environment before any device is deployed
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0813: Denial of Control - a process-state outcome (the emergent consequence of other techniques, such as blocked commands or manipulated parameters), not a discrete event a log source records directly. Confirmed via the ICS ATT&CK matrix structure itself: Impact-tactic 'Loss of X'/'Denial of X'/'Manipulation of X' techniques describe consequences an analyst infers by correlating other technique-level evidence (e.g. T0836 Modify Parameter, T1691 Block OT Message), not something with its own independent log signature.
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0815: Denial of View - same reasoning as T0813: a process-state outcome inferred from other technique evidence, not an independently loggable event
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0826: Loss of Availability - same reasoning as T0813
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0827: Loss of Control - same reasoning as T0813
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0828: Loss of Productivity and Revenue - a business/financial consequence, not a technical event any log source records
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0829: Loss of View - same reasoning as T0813
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0831: Manipulation of Control - same reasoning as T0813
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0832: Manipulation of View - same reasoning as T0813
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0837: Loss of Protection - same reasoning as T0813 (a safety-system-state outcome, not a discrete logged event)
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0879: Damage to Property - a physical-world consequence, not a technical event any log source records
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0880: Loss of Safety - same reasoning as T0813 (a safety-system-state outcome)
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0860: Wireless Compromise - requires wireless spectrum/RF monitoring, the same fundamentally different monitoring capability already noted for T1669 Wi-Fi Networks (Enterprise)
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0887: Wireless Sniffing - requires wireless spectrum/RF monitoring, same reasoning as T0860
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T0842: Network Sniffing - an adversary passively capturing traffic is by definition not observable by the victim's own log sources - same reasoning as Enterprise T1040
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T1695.001: Block Communications: Serial COM - serial-line jamming/disconnection is a physical-layer concern; passive Ethernet-tap OT network monitoring (the only OT network visibility this catalog has) cannot observe serial communications
out_of_scope.ics-attack:T1695.003: Block Communications: Wi-Fi - requires wireless spectrum/RF monitoring, same reasoning as T0860/T0887
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1406.001: Steganography - requires content/statistical analysis, same reasoning as Enterprise T1027.003
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1406.002: Software Packing - requires static binary analysis, same reasoning as Enterprise T1027.002
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1516: Input Injection - a malicious app programmatically injecting input into other apps' UI is an internal app-to-app behavior, not observable via MDM/MTD/forensic evidence without deep OS-level instrumentation not confirmed available on mobile
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1541: Foreground Persistence - an app's internal self-management of its own process priority/lifecycle, not an externally observable event
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1575: Native API - internal API call usage within a malicious app's own process, not observable without deep runtime instrumentation not confirmed available
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1617: Hooking - internal app-level API hooking, not observable via any confirmed evidence source in this catalog
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1627: Execution Guardrails - malware checking its environment before acting, an internal pre-execution self-check - same reasoning as Enterprise T1480
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1627.001: Geofencing - same reasoning as parent T1627: an internal pre-execution self-check
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1628: Hide Artifacts - internal app self-concealment behavior within its own sandboxed storage, not observable via confirmed evidence sources
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1628.001: Suppress Application Icon - same reasoning as parent T1628
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1628.002: User Evasion - same reasoning as parent T1628
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1628.003: Conceal Multimedia Files - same reasoning as parent T1628
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1629.001: Prevent Application Removal - internal app self-protection behavior; T1629.003 (Disable or Modify Tools) is covered via MDM lost-check-in evidence, but preventing its OWN uninstallation specifically is not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1629.002: Device Lockout - an internal malicious action with no confirmed distinct observable signature beyond the lockscreen state itself
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1630.002: File Deletion - internal app behavior; the base T1662 Data Destruction is covered via Cellebrite's confirmed deleted-data-recovery capability, but detecting the deletion ACT itself as it happens is not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1630.003: Disguise Root/Jailbreak Indicators - an internal app behavior specifically designed to defeat the same jailbreak/root detection this catalog's MTD sources rely on
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1631: Process Injection - internal app-level process injection, not observable without deep runtime instrumentation not confirmed available on mobile OSes
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1631.001: Ptrace System Calls - same reasoning as parent T1631
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1633: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion - malware checking its environment before acting, an internal pre-execution self-check - same reasoning as Enterprise T1497
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1633.001: System Checks - same reasoning as parent T1633
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1414: Clipboard Data - internal app API access to transient clipboard content, not confirmed observable via any source in this catalog
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1417: Input Capture - internal app-level input capture, would require deep runtime instrumentation not confirmed available on mobile
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1417.001: Keylogging - same reasoning as parent T1417
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1417.002: GUI Input Capture - same reasoning as parent T1417
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1429: Audio Capture - internal app API access to the microphone, not confirmed observable via any source in this catalog

out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1513: Screen Capture - internal app API access to the screen, same reasoning as T1429
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1517: Access Notifications - internal app access to notification content; not among Cellebrite's confirmed extraction categories and not confirmed observable elsewhere
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1616: Call Control - internal app-level programmatic call manipulation, not confirmed observable via any source in this catalog
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1676: Linked Devices - exploitation of a paired companion device (e.g. smartwatch) is a distinct architecture this catalog has no researched evidence source for
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1634: Credentials from Password Store - internal app-level access to the OS keychain/credential store API, not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1634.001: Keychain - same reasoning as parent T1634
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1635: Steal Application Access Token - internal app-level token theft, not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1635.001: URI Hijacking - internal app-level intent/URI interception, not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1398: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts - a malicious app's manifest-level boot-receiver registration, a static app property not confirmed observable via any runtime evidence source in this catalog
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1603: Scheduled Task/Job - internal app-level task scheduling API usage, not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1624: Event Triggered Execution - internal app-level event-handler registration, not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1624.001: Broadcast Receivers - same reasoning as parent T1624
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1625: Hijack Execution Flow - internal app-level execution flow manipulation, not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1625.001: System Runtime API Hijacking - same reasoning as parent T1625
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1645: Compromise Client Software Binary - trojanizing a legitimate app's binary; related to the already-covered T1406 (Obfuscated Files) forensic-examination reasoning, but binary-tampering detection specifically was not confirmed as a distinct capability
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1641: Data Manipulation - in-app or in-transit data tampering, not confirmed observable via any source in this catalog
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1641.001: Transmitted Data Manipulation - same reasoning as Enterprise T1565.002: requires in-transit content inspection beyond what any source here provides
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1582: SMS Control - programmatic SMS send/intercept is an internal app-level behavior; downstream evidence (unusual SMS present) is covered by the already-established T1636.004, but the active control technique itself is not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1430: Location Tracking - internal app-level GPS/location API access, not confirmed observable via any source in this catalog
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1430.002: Impersonate SS7 Nodes - a telecom-carrier-infrastructure-level attack entirely outside any source in this catalog, same category as T1451 SIM Card Swap
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1458: Replication Through Removable Media - Android SecurityLog's confirmed evidence is specifically 'harmful adb commands,' not general USB file-transfer monitoring; not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1474: Supply Chain Compromise - occurs upstream of the victim's environment, same reasoning as Enterprise T1195
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1474.001: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools - same reasoning as parent T1474
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1474.002: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain - physical, occurs entirely outside the victim's environment, same reasoning as Enterprise T1195.003
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1474.003: Compromise Software Supply Chain - same reasoning as parent T1474
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1623: Command and Scripting Interpreter - on-device local shell execution (not via ADB/USB) is not covered by Android SecurityLog's confirmed ADB-command-only evidence
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1623.001: Unix Shell - same reasoning as parent T1623
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1521.003: SSL Pinning - describes an app's own defensive behavior being bypassed by an attacker; the bypass itself is an internal app-level event, not confirmed observable
out_of_scope.mobile-attack:T1407: Download New Code at Runtime - an internal app-runtime behavior; no source in this catalog has confirmed evidence of detecting this specific pattern distinct from general app-risk scanning
